text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "Reweighting weights are computed as w_i = exp(-β(U_θ(S_i) − U_θ̂(S_i))) normalized by the sum of the same exponential terms over all retained states [W3168247670#005]. They are derived from state probabilities p_θ(S_i) ~ exp(-βH(S_i)), where H is the Hamiltonian (potential plus kinetic energy) and β = 1/(k_B T) [W3168247670#005]. The kinetic energy cancels because it appears identically in the numerator and denominator of the probability ratio p_θ/p_θ̂, so only the potential energy difference remains [W3168247670#005]. For θ = θ̂ the weights reduce to 1/N, recovering the plain time average [W3168247670#005]."}
